The disclosure describes a validation objective, not a completed validation result or approved medical device.

organization.name: Canadian Strategic Missions Corporation
organization.description: Canadian Strategic Missions Corporation is a Waterloo-based Canadian space and defence technology company developing dual-use systems for strategic power, remote and Arctic operations, space resources, water purification and advanced sensing.
organization.ownership: Corporations Canada lists the corporation as Active and Daniel Sax as the sole current individual with significant control, holding more than 75 percent of shares indirectly. The federal lobby registry reports no parent company. The corporate record also warns that two consecutive annual filings are overdue and a notice of intent to dissolve has been sent; recheck before publication.
organization.disclosed_financing_summary: Public records separately identify a C$1 million CSA LEUNR project, a C$1 million National Defence IDEaS project, C$169,000 for DIANA Mission Control, C$1.2 million within a C$3 million NGen manufacturing project, C$5 million within a C$10.4 million ERA project, and C$4.5 million within a C$10,095,066 FedDev project. These figures have different program and project bases and are not summed as financing or revenue.
organization.defence_posture: National Defence funds LEUNR R&D under the NORAD Modernization Science and Technology Contest, and CSMC is in NATO DIANA's 2026 cohort for remote monitoring of micro modular reactors. FedDev separately supports a project framed for Arctic defence and remote energy. These grants, selections and development projects do not establish procurement, fielding, customer acceptance or operational reactor use.
organization.dual_use_posture: CSMC positions LEUNR for remote civil power, Canadian defence and Arctic infrastructure, nuclear research and lunar surface systems. Government and partner records support these as funded development contexts, while no reviewed source establishes a licensed operating reactor, named community or defence customer, power-delivery agreement, Indigenous partnership, or deployed site.

profile_data.operatingModel: CSMC presents CSMC Nuclear as its wholly owned strategic-power subsidiary and CSMC Labs as its wholly owned R&D division for quantum, natural resources and other deep technologies.
profile_data.portfolioScope: Development-stage micro-nuclear reactors; lunar water purification and resource processing; portable multi-sensor imaging; quantum-gravimetry sensing; and broader R&D in robotics, nanomaterials, electrochemistry, industrial automation and space systems.
profile_data.currentActivity: Current public activity includes a $10.095 million FedDev-supported microreactor project, National Defence and CSA LEUNR projects, the Aqualunar-winning LunaPure system, lunar architecture studies and a company-reported Luxembourg QASM contract.
profile_data.evidenceBoundary: Technology descriptions, awards and programs are source-backed. Maturity labels are preserved, and mission matches are derived analyst assessments rather than procurement eligibility, endorsement, customer interest or classified demand.
profile_data.canadianFootprint: FedDev Ontario describes the company as Waterloo-based in July 2026. Canadian Space Agency and other federal records also identify Toronto activity under the current and former names.
profile_data.foundedAndIdentity: Incorporated in 2020 as Canadian Space Mining Corporation and renamed Canadian Strategic Missions Corporation in December 2025, with the federal name record registered in January 2026.

organization.current_activity: On July 23, 2026, FedDev Ontario announced a $4.5 million contribution toward CSMC's $10.095 million micro-nuclear power development project for Arctic defence operations and remote energy applications.
organization.operating_context: CSMC operates through CSMC Nuclear and CSMC Labs. Public LEUNR work spans conceptual and detailed design, representative unfuelled analogue and simulator activity, instrumentation and controls, a planned manufacturing cell, remote-monitoring software and lunar-power architecture studies. These workstreams are development evidence; they do not establish a CNSC licence, fueled criticality, an operating site, serial production or commercial delivery.
organization.canadian_footprint: FedDev describes CSMC as Waterloo-based.
